text:
Los Angeles is 5-10-2 with 12 points, and if any team in the league has a case that the table is lying, it's this one. The Kings own 51.5% of the expected goals, and our numbers say they've earned 19.2 points, about seven more than they have. Their last three games were all losses, outscored 13-4, while they took 57% of the chances. Our playoff race still gives them 28%.

The reason is in the crease. Darcy Kuemper is .847 over his last five starts, 6.4 goals worse than expected, and the team has allowed 9.4 more goals than its shots against deserved.

Peter Laviolette was hired in June to open up the offense, and the reunion with Artemi Panarin is working. Panarin, Adrian Kempe and Alex Laferriere take 61% of the expected goals at 5-on-5 and have outscored opponents 8-3. Kempe passed Dustin Brown on the franchise scoring list with a hat trick against San Jose. Brandt Clarke, paired with Erik Gustafsson, is having the breakout season people have waited for (62% of expected goals together).

And Corey Perry, at 41, is still scoring and still dropping the gloves. Watch Kuemper's next few starts. If the saves come back to average, this team's chance numbers say the wins should follow.
headline: The Kings deserve better than their record
